pronunciation.notes: The be is short and unstressed, like the 'a' in 'about'. Stress kom.

word.shortDefinition: To get something that comes to you.

intro.title: The word that looks like 'become'
paragraphs: A tourist in a Berlin café says to the waiter: Ich bekomme ein Steak. He means 'I'll have a steak'. If he were thinking in English, it would sound like 'I become a steak.'
Bekommen looks almost exactly like the English word 'become', but it means 'get' or 'receive'. It's the most famous false friend in German, and you'll use it every day.

etymology.title: Where it comes from

parts.meaning: a prefix that points at a target
parts.note: It doesn't add much meaning on its own.
The same kommen as in ankommen.

etymology.summary: Originally both words meant 'to come to, to reach'. In German, the meaning became 'something comes to you', so you get it. In English, 'become' drifted toward 'come to be'.

bonus.note: This is the German word you actually want for 'become': Ich werde müde, I'm getting tired.

tables.title: Present tense
tables.intro: Bekommen follows kommen, so it's regular in the present.
notes: The past participle is bekommen, with no ge-. Verbs starting with be- never add ge.

keyTrap.title: The big trap: bekommen is not 'become'
keyTrap.explanation: When you mean 'become' or 'get' in the sense of changing, German uses werden. Bekommen is only for receiving something.

wrong.verdict: This means nothing. You can't receive 'tired'.

commonMistakes.title: No ge- in the past
commonMistakes.explanation: Verbs starting with be-, ge-, er-, ver- and zer- don't add ge in the Perfekt.

commonMistakes.title: Ordering food
commonMistakes.explanation: In a restaurant, bekommen is the polite way to order. Ich will sounds demanding.

commonMistakes.title: Who gets what
commonMistakes.explanation: From a waiter, 'Was bekommen Sie?' means 'What will you have?'. When you pay, 'Was bekommen Sie von mir?' means 'How much do I owe you?'.

sampleSentences.german: Ich bekomme ein Glas Wasser, bitte.
sampleSentences.english: I'll have a glass of water, please.

sampleSentences.german: Das Medikament bekommen Sie in jeder Apotheke.
sampleSentences.english: You can get the medicine at any pharmacy.

quiz.prompt: Im Winter ___ es früh dunkel. (bekommen or werden?)
quiz.fullAnswer: Im Winter wird es früh dunkel.
quiz.explanation: Getting dark is a change of state, so it's werden.
Receiving, and no ge- in the past.

quiz.prompt: You're in a café. How do you order a coffee politely?
quiz.explanation: Ich hätte gern einen Kaffee also works.

quiz.prompt: What does Sie bekommt ein Baby mean?

memoryHook: Bekommen is what comes to you. If you're changing, you werden. If something arrives, you bekommen.
